title: GPU pool pressure: hysteresis miscalibration, abortive prefetch amplification, and admission tuning
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Summary: During a hosted-GPU capacity event on 2025-02-16 we observed sustained queue growth and elevated p95/p99 latencies despite autoscaler activity. Investigation showed a confluence of issues: (1) an aggressive prefetch path that spawned abortive downstream work on overloaded pools (we call this "abortive prefetch amplification"), (2) autoscaler hysteresis thresholds that delayed scale-up while queues accumulated, and (3) admission gating that allowed small requests to accumulate in a way that amplified head-of-line blocking for large, long-running requests. This ticket captures follow-up fixes, verification, and runbook updates.
root_cause: Autoscaler hysteresis thresholds were tuned to avoid flapping for normal load, but during a burst the time-to-scale-up exceeded the time for queue compaction and starvation. Simultaneously, the prefetch subsystem attempted to warm KV/cache shards for many concurrent sessions; when GPUs reported high load the prefetches were aborted and left short-lived tasks occupying admission slots without progressing (abortive prefetch amplification). Admission policies prioritized request count over effective token-time occupancy, causing head-of-line blocking. Monitoring lacked a clear signal that coupled prefetch abort rates + inflight token-seconds would predict imminent exhaustion.
impact_summary: Between 2025-02-16 03:12 and 2025-02-16 03:48 UTC: p95 latency increased by ~2.3x, p99 by ~3.1x for hosted text-generation endpoints; token cost rose ~18% due to repeated prefetch+retry cycles; several customers saw timeouts and automatic retry storms. No data exfiltration. Revenue impact limited but developer experience degraded for PLG signups during the window.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: Manually increased autoscaler aggressiveness for affected pools (temporary override) to force scale-up
Enabled emergency-prefetch-disable flag for the prefetch path to stop abortive work
Put conservative tenant-level request caps to reduce fanout from heavy tenants
Rolled back a configuration change to admission timeouts that increased concurrent request allowances
proposed_action_items: Tune autoscaler: reduce scale-up hysteresis for burst-prone pools and add surge window metric (inflight token-seconds) to trigger faster warm-ups
Add a prefetch backpressure mechanism: limit concurrent prefetches per shard and make prefetch use non-blocking low-priority admission slots with robust cancellation accounting
Admission controller rewrite: track token-time occupancy (estimated GPU-seconds) rather than raw concurrent request count for fair-share decisions
Implement an "allocation credit" circuit breaker that demotes tenants exceeding fanout-to-progress ratio for 1 minute
Add an automated emergency prewarm flow: detect rising surge signal and opportunistically spin minimal burst nodes using a warm image, without full autoscaler commit
Create deterministic test harness that replays abortive-prefetch scenarios against staging to validate admission changes
Add dashboards + alert: prefetch abort rate, inflight token-seconds, sustained-scale-delay, and tenant-fanout ratio; tie to incident runbook alerts
Update runbook: include decision tree for prefetch disable, emergency prewarm, tenant capping, and how to revert admission policy changes
implementation_notes: We will land incremental changes to minimize blast radius: first disable prefetch by default behind a feature flag and route a small internal cohort to the new admission heuristics. Next deploy autoscaler hysteresis adjustments behind runtime flags and enable the surge-window metric. All changes require end-to-end staging verification with the synthetic traffic harness before canary to production.
verification_plan: Stage tests: replay incident traffic profile with synthetic clients including high-fanout tenants; measure prefetch aborts and queue depth
Canary rollout for admission heuristics to <5% of pools; monitor p95/p99 and cpu/gpu utilization for 48h
Autoscaler hysteresis changes: run A/B with and without surge window metric for 72h; validate no increase in flapping and improved speed-to-scale metrics
Post-deploy chaos: simulate node drain and validate that emergency prewarm + new admission prevents queue amplification

notes_and_discussion: 2025-02-18: Postmortem reviewed with SRE, Runtime, and Product; consensus that prefetch should be deprioritized under high queue pressure (Ava, Maya, Eitan)
2025-02-20: Security reviewed the emergency prewarm design; no keys/hardware exposure concerns (security signoff by Lena Ortiz)
2025-02-25: Design review suggested a two-phase admission rollout to avoid latency regressions for small requests (Design: Priya Kaur)
2025-02-28: Benchmarks show token-time accounting reduces head-of-line blocking in synthetic tests by ~45% compared to request-count admission
close_criteria: All action items implemented or have tracked follow-ups with owners; staging+canary verification passed; dashboards and runbook updated; no recurrence in 30 days for pools with new config
